architecture.description: MLP surrogate of log10(Pv) as a function of (log10 f, log10 Bpk); SYNTHETIC training surface.
architecture.name: steinmetz-surrogate-mlp-2x8x8x1

description: Demonstrates the verified inference workflow of the data-driven adapter (sha256-checked weights, normalisation, numpy MLP inference). Target: log10(Pv) = f(log10 f, log10 Bpk) of a SYNTHETIC Steinmetz surface.

known_limitations: SYNTHETIC surrogate: trained on a power law with illustrative parameters, not on measured data; it does not describe any real material.
No temperature dependence and no DC-bias dependence are modelled.
Sinusoidal-excitation Steinmetz surface only; the surrogate interpolates inside the training grid (20-500 kHz, 20-300 mT) and must not be extrapolated.
numerical_constraints: frequency and flux_density_peak must be strictly positive (log10 input features)

identity.name: Reference ANN surrogate of a SYNTHETIC Steinmetz surface

sources.note: Origin of the power-law loss description; only the functional form Pv = k f^alpha Bpk^beta is used, with SYNTHETIC parameter values.
sources.reference: C. P. Steinmetz, 'On the law of hysteresis', Transactions of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers, vol. IX, no. 1, pp. 1-64, 1892 (reprinted in Proc. IEEE, vol. 72, no. 2, pp. 197-221, 1984)

sources.locator: Eq. (1): classical Steinmetz equation Pv = k f^alpha B^beta
sources.note: Reference for the classical Steinmetz form used as the synthetic training surface.
sources.reference: J. Reinert, A. Brockmeyer, R. W. De Doncker, 'Calculation of losses in ferro- and ferrimagnetic materials based on the modified Steinmetz equation', IEEE Trans. Ind. Appl., vol. 37, no. 4, pp. 1055-1061, 2001

sources.note: synthetic - chosen only for a ferrite-like order of magnitude
sources.reference: SYNTHETIC illustrative parameter set k=2.0, alpha=1.45, beta=2.6 (Pv in W/m^3, f in Hz, Bpk in T); not a measured or datasheet material

sources.note: synthetic training data generated by the script itself; weights file digest in sha256
sources.reference: benchmarks/fit_reference_mlp.py: numpy MLP fitted with scipy L-BFGS-B, seed 20261019, full-batch, on the synthetic grid

features.inputs: log10 then z-score (NormalizationSpec kind='log10' with mean/std)

optimizer.message: CONVERGENCE: RELATIVE REDUCTION OF F <= FACTR*EPSMCH

synthetic_parameters.units: Pv W/m^3, f Hz, Bpk T

weights.note: dense layer list (W out x in, b, activation) as JSON lists; no binary blobs

source.note: synthetic training data generated by the script itself; weights file digest in sha256
